feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 6 & 1 \\ 8 & 1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 9 & -5 & 4 \\ 4 & 5 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 3 & 1 \\ -12 & -24 & -13 & 5 \\ -16 & -11 & -17 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations 

- ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-4{C}_{4}$
- ${C}_{2}:=…$
- ${C}_{3}:=…$

each of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{4},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?
feedback.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left of ${a}_{44}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 6 & 1 \\ 8 & 1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 9 & -5 & 4 \\ 4 & 5 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-4{C}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 6 & 1 \\ -12 & 1 & 2 & 5 \\ -16 & 9 & -5 & 4 \\ 0 & 5 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-5{C}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 6 & 1 \\ -12 & -24 & 2 & 5 \\ -16 & -11 & -5 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-3{C}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 3 & 1 \\ -12 & -24 & -13 & 5 \\ -16 & -11 & -17 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-5{C}_{4}\,$ and $\,{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-3{C}_{4}.$
